name: Pekah
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Pekah the son of Remaliah, his own captain, conspired against him and smote him in the palace of the king's house with fifty men of the Gileadites, and reigned in his room.
Pekah, a captain of his, conspires against him and smites him in the king's house at Samaria with fifty Gileadites, then reigns in his room.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: “But Pekah the son of Remaliah, a captain of his, conspired against him”: Pekahiah’s own captain conspired against him, smote him in the palace of the king’s house, killed him and reigned in his room.

note.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?

points: Pekah the son of Remaliah reigned twenty years in Samaria, and he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord. Evil again.
Pekah son of Remaliah reigns twenty years over Israel, the same Pekah spoken of in the book of Isaiah.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: “In the two and fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria”: the fifty-second year, the last year of Uzziah’s reign.

note.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?

points: “In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath–pileser king of Assyria”: the same Pul we read about earlier, same guy, the Third. He took Gilead, Galilee and “all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.” This is the first wave. The first wave of the Northern Kingdom being deported out of the land and taken into Assyria was right here; it was done in waves. Pekah began to reign in the fifty-second year of Uzziah, and Pul conquered the Northern Kingdom at this time.

note.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?

points: Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah, smote him, slew him and reigned in his stead. The trend is still running right up to the captivity.
Hoshea son of Elah conspires against Pekah, smites and slays him, and reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: In those days the Most High begins to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: “In those days the Lord began to send against Judah Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah”: Pekah is Ephraim. This is during Ahaz’s reign.
Rezin king of Syria and Pekah king of Israel come up to war against Jerusalem and besiege Ahaz but cannot overcome him.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: “Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to war”. When Ahaz was going into his idolatry, Pekah and Rezin got together and made an alliance to go against Judah, because by this time Judah’s going the hell off.

note.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?

points: In the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up toward Jerusalem to war, but could not prevail against it.

note.label: Isaiah 7: Ahaz, the Confederacy, and the Sign of Immanuel

points: The same history as 2 Kings 16, in more detail: “in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah”, “Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.”

note.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?
